theater: 美索不達米亞巴比倫城

battle.name: 巴比倫的洗劫
battle.theater: 美索不達米亞巴比倫城
battle.brief: 公元前1595年，赫梯王穆爾希利一世自安納托利亞南下，沿幼發拉底河打到兩河腹地，攻破巴比倫城，掠走馬爾杜克神像與西帕爾的伊什塔爾銅像。遠征軍配的是銅矛、銅斧、複合弓與蒙皮楯，攻城靠工兵掘地道破牆；卡面的埃及長矛，正是這條青銅矛兵技術路線的遠祖。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場衝突發生在公元前1595年的兩河中游，攻守雙方都是王國級別。進攻方是赫梯王國的舊王國時期，國都在安納托利亞高原的哈圖沙（今土耳其博阿茲柯伊一帶的布亞茲卡萊），國王是穆爾希利一世。赫梯此時的軍事結構是「王帶著眾王」：哈圖沙王室的直屬兵，與臣屬國王、附庸部族的首領各率本部來會，戰爭的規模取決於能召集多少盟友、多少輛牛車，以及盟邦能供應多少糧食與役畜。防守方是巴比倫王國第一王朝，即漢穆拉比所建的阿摩利特王朝的都城；國王西布卡德—舒什是這條王朝的末代君主，王國的骨架是王宮、埃薩吉拉神廟與其附屬莊園、城牆工役與神職人員組成的城市國家。巴比倫位於幼發拉底河中游東岸，控制著通往波斯灣的商路與南部的水利灌溉，此時它的北方防線就是河中游的敘利亞諸城，與赫梯的邊界在河上對峙多年。戰局之外還有第三股力量：來自伊朗札格羅斯山區的加喜特人，早已在東面邊境上活動，《巴比倫王表》記王朝末段正是加喜特人接掌王位。敘利亞北部的胡里諸邦——哈蘇瓦、卡爾凱美什、阿勒頗——既是赫梯南下的通道，也首當其衝。
countriesEn: This clash took place in the middle Euphrates in 1595 BC, and both sides were kingdoms in their own right. The attacking side was the Hittite kingdom in its Old Kingdom phase, its capital at Hattusa on the Anatolian plateau (in the neighbourhood of today's Boğazköy, at Büyükkale), under King Mursili I. Hittite military organisation at this time was a king leading a company of kings: the direct troops of the house of Hattusa, and the rulers of subject states and the chiefs of dependent tribes each bringing their own contingent, so that the size of a war was settled by how many allies could be mustered, how many ox carts could be found, and how much grain and how many draught animals the allies could supply. The defending side was the city of Babylon, capital of the first Babylonian dynasty, the Amorite dynasty founded by Hammurabi; its king was Sibkadd-Sheš, the last ruler of that line, and the skeleton of the state was the royal palace, the temple of Esagila with its estates, the labour gangs assigned to the walls, and the priesthood. Babylon stood on the east bank of the middle Euphrates, controlling the trade road to the Persian Gulf and the irrigation of the south; its northern defence line at this time was the Syrian city-states of the middle river, and the frontier with the Hittites had faced each other across that river for years. A third force stood outside the battle: the Kassites, who came from the Zagros mountains of Iran and had been active on the eastern frontier for some time; the Babylonian King List records that it was the Kassites who took the throne at the end of the dynasty. The Hurrian states of northern Syria — Hassuwa, Carchemish, Aleppo — were both the corridor by which the Hittites marched south and the first to bear the brunt.
people: 留下姓名的核心是穆爾希利一世。他是赫梯舊王國第三代君主，祖父拉巴爾納一世原是哈圖蘇伊的首領，奪取哈圖沙後開創王朝；穆爾希利把都城正式遷到哈圖沙，完成了赫梯人從內陸走向安納托利亞中部要地的轉身，先後發動敘利亞遠征與對哈蘇瓦的戰役，最後才是沿幼發拉底河直取巴比倫的這一次。巴比倫方面留下名字的是西布卡德—舒什，《巴比倫王表A》記他是雅金之子、「未滿一年而終」，這條簡短的註記正好對應城破之後王統中斷、國王本人下落不明的情形。往後的編年文本提到加喜特人入主巴比倫，並提到一位名叫圖什拉塔的加喜特君主，很可能就是趁虛而入的那一位。哈圖沙的宮廷檔案裡保存一封署名穆爾希利一世的信，寫給巴比倫國王，敘述渡河、攻城與奪走馬爾杜克神像，並表示願以贖金換回神像；這封信是後世重建此次遠征細節的主要依據之一。赫梯方面還有他的兒子哈圖西里一世，繼位後延續父王的遠征方向，《哈圖西里一世自辯書》殘片與記錄瘟疫饑饑的《解縛之歌》都繫於他即位初年，把巴比倫之劫說成神明降怒的懲罰。巴比倫城內的祭司與占卜士群體也值得一提：埃薩吉拉的馬爾杜克祭司團掌握王朝的祭祀與曆算，這批人留下的占卜與天象抄本，後來成了赫梯人帶走的物件之一。
peopleEn: The central name is Mursili I. He was the third ruler of the Hittite Old Kingdom; his grandfather Labarna I had begun as a chief at Hattusi, and after seizing Hattusa founded the dynasty. Mursili formally moved the capital to Hattusa, completing the Hittite turn from the interior towards the key sites of central Anatolia, and he led in turn the campaign in Syria, the war against Hassuwa, and last of all this march down the Euphrates to Babylon. On the Babylonian side the name that survives is Sibkadd-Sheš: the Babylonian King List A records him as the son of Yakin, who did not complete his year, and that short note corresponds exactly to the interruption of the royal line and the disappearance of the king himself once the city had fallen. The later chronicle text records the Kassites taking Babylon and gives the name of a Kassite ruler, Tushratta, who may well be the man who moved in to fill the vacancy. The archive of Hattusa preserves a letter in the name of Mursili I addressed to the king of Babylon, describing the crossing of the river, the siege and the taking of the statue of Marduk, and offering to give the statue back for a ransom; that letter is one of the main foundations for reconstructing the details of this campaign. On the Hittite side there is also his son Hattusili I, who continued the direction of his father's campaigns; the fragmentary Apology of Hattusili I and the Song of Release, which records plague and famine, are both placed at the beginning of his reign and read the sack of Babylon as a punishment sent by the gods. The body of Babylonian priests and diviners deserves a mention too: the Marduk priesthood of Esagila controlled the sacrifices and the calendar of the dynasty, and the divinatory and astronomical copies left by these men were among the things carried away by the Hittites.
kits: 卡面上這把埃及長矛並不在哈圖沙的軍械庫裡：它是早王朝時期的埃及長矛，銅或青銅矛頭安在木桿上，埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。它說明的是一條技術路線，即把金屬矛頭裝在長桿上，讓刺擊的力量由肩背一路傳到尖端。巴比倫城頭與城下的長矛正是這一路線的兩河流域版本，銅矛頭分柄套式與柄穿式兩種，工藝上與埃及晚王朝的長矛同屬一類。巴比倫的近戰裝備還有銅斧、窄刃銅匕首，攻城用的撞槌與鎬，遠射以弓箭為主，擲石與投槍並用，東面邊境的加喜特人另以投石索著稱。赫梯方面的兵器同樣以銅質為主：矛、斧、匕首，配以木芯包皮的複合弓——安納托利亞出土的早期複合弓殘件，是世界上最早的這類證據之一；防護是木框蒙皮的楯與皮甲；攻堅靠工兵掘地道、架活動塔與撞槌，輔以拆毀牆基的作業；運輸用牛拉的車與驢隊，一支遠征軍真正的瓶頸是馬匹與飼料。馬爾杜克與伊什塔爾的神像本身也是戰利品：這場洗劫把巴比倫的儀式器具與泥板文書一併帶走，哈圖沙檔案中那件被學者稱為「穆爾希利文本」的泥板，就是一份巴比倫占卜系列的赫梯抄本，學界有一種流行解釋，認為它正是1595年自巴比倫帶走的戰利品。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card was not in the armoury of Hattusa. It is a spear of the Egyptian Early Dynastic period, a copper or bronze head fixed to a wooden shaft, used by the Egyptians to hold city walls and later to recover lost ground. What it represents is a line of technique: fitting a metal head to a long shaft so that the force of the thrust travels from shoulder and back to the point. The spears of the walls and streets of Babylon were the Mesopotamian version of that same line, with copper heads made either with a socket for the shaft or with a tang passed through it, technically of a kind with the spears of Egypt's later dynasties. Babylon's close-combat equipment also included copper axes and narrow-bladed copper daggers, with rams and picks for the walls, while the missile weapons were chiefly the bow and arrow, with stones and javelins thrown in support; the Kassites on the eastern frontier were noted for the sling. The Hittite arms were likewise mostly copper: spears, axes and daggers, with the composite bow of wood and horn or sinew — the early composite bow fragments from Anatolia are among the oldest such evidence in the world. Protection was the hide-covered wooden frame shield and leather armour; siege work was the business of sappers, who drove mines, moved towers and rams, and undermined the foot of the walls. Transport was by ox cart and donkey train, and the real constraint on a distant expedition was horses and fodder. The statues of Marduk and Ishtar were themselves part of the booty: the sack carried off Babylon's ritual furniture and its clay tablets along with everything else, and the tablet in the Hattusa archive that scholars call the Mursili text is a Hittite copy of a Babylonian omen series; a popular interpretation holds that it was among the things carried out of Babylon in 1595.
tactics: 赫梯人的遠征有一套固定程序：在安納托利亞集結，再以連續攻勢沿幼發拉底河一個城邦接一個城邦地推進，每到一處便強攻城牆、拆毀宮殿、掠走財物，而不打算長期治理。穆爾希利一世的戰役順序是敘利亞線（攻破阿勒頗、焚其王宮）、哈蘇瓦線（擒其國王），最後才是巴比倫。渡河是全軍最關鍵的技術動作：幼發拉底河在春天水勢較低，赫梯人靠淺灘涉渡與臨時舟橋通過，渡過之後立即在對岸紮營，把城牆一段一段壓縮。攻城用兩種手段並用：一是正面強攻，密集的盾陣貼牆、弓箭壓制城頭；二是工兵在夜裡掘地道破壞牆基，必要時以撞槌撞開缺口，再由缺口湧入。城破之後的處置快速而有目的：主要城區被焚，神廟財物與神像被搬走，王宮的文書櫃連同泥板一起被帶走，隨後全軍帶著戰利品撤回安納托利亞，不留駐軍。對巴比倫人而言更致命的是戰後的權力真空：赫梯人走了，加喜特人來了，防務、灌溉與行政在很長一段時間裡沒有重建，宮室與神廟的經濟體系中斷，繁盛的巴比倫在接下來一兩代裡人口外流，直到加喜特王朝把它重新聚起。
tacticsEn: The Hittite expedition followed a fixed routine: they mustered in Anatolia, then advanced in a series of attacks along the Euphrates from one city-state to the next, and at each place stormed the walls, stripped the palace and carried off the wealth, without any intention of governing what they had taken. The order of Mursili I's campaigns runs along the Syrian line, with the taking of Aleppo and the burning of its royal palace, then the line of Hassuwa, whose king was captured, and last of all Babylon. The crossing of the river was the most critical technical action of the whole march: the Euphrates runs low in spring, and the Hittites passed by fording the shallows and by temporary bridges, and once across they encamped on the far bank at once and pressed the walls section by section. Two methods were used together in the siege: frontal assault, with dense shield walls brought up against the defences and bows covering the parapet; and the work of sappers, who drove mines into the foot of the wall at night and, where necessary, broke a breach with the ram and poured in through it. Once the city was taken, the disposal of it was quick and purposeful: the main quarters were burned, the temple treasure and the images were carried off, the document chests of the palace went with the clay tablets, and then the whole army withdrew to Anatolia with its booty and left no garrison. For the Babylonians the more mortal blow came after the battle, in the vacuum of power: the Hittites went home and the Kassites came in, and for a long stretch the defences, the irrigation works and the administration were not rebuilt. The economic system of palace and temple broke down, and the flourishing city shed population for a generation or two, until the Kassite dynasty gathered it up again.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。第一類是文獻自述：年份為公元前1595年，另按不同年代學方案有前1596年或前1593年之說；季候多半落在春季作戰期，但存世的巴比倫編年文本沒有保存下可確定的月份，所以本篇只作春季重建。赫梯舊王國的年代約在公元前1650年至前1500年，穆爾希利一世在位的推算約為前1620年至前1590年。巴比倫第一王朝在《巴比倫王表A》中共列二十一位君主，漢穆拉比一系的統治自前1792年延續到前1750年（中等年代學），末代君主西布卡德—舒什的年數記為不足一年。遠征距離方面，自哈圖沙至巴比倫的直線距離約一千一百至一千二百公里，沿幼發拉底河的行軍路程更長，途中至少要跨越這條大河兩次。加喜特人治巴比倫約四百四十年，大致自前1595年到前1155年，終於伊蘭國王舒特魯克—納洪特的攻入。西帕爾的伊什塔爾銅像高約一點八米，現藏巴比倫的伊拉克博物館，其銘文自記在1595年被帶往哈圖沙。第三類是推估，必須打折扣：巴比倫城郭面積常被估為三百公頃上下，城內人口在漢穆拉比時代多被估在數萬至十萬之間；赫梯遠征軍的確切人數沒有任何文獻依據，舊王國時期的相關估算只能在數千至數萬之間浮動，可信度有限。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first class is what the documents say of themselves. The date is 1595 BC, with 1596 BC and 1593 BC proposed under other chronologies; the season of the campaign was most probably the spring campaigning period, but the surviving Babylonian chronicle does not preserve a datable month, so this account reconstructs the spring and no more. The Hittite Old Kingdom is dated roughly from 1650 to 1500 BC, and the reign of Mursili I is put at about 1620 to 1590 BC. The first Babylonian dynasty lists twenty-one rulers in the Babylonian King List A; the rule of the line of Hammurabi runs from 1792 to 1750 BC on the middle chronology, and the years of the last ruler, Sibkadd-Sheš, are given as less than a full year. As for distance, the direct line from Hattusa to Babylon is on the order of eleven to twelve hundred kilometres, the marching route along the Euphrates is longer, and the river itself has to be crossed at least twice on the way. Kassite rule at Babylon lasted about four hundred and forty years, roughly from 1595 to 1155 BC, and ended with the entry of Shutruk-Nahhunte of Elam. The bronze Ishtar of Sippar stands about one metre and eighty centimetres high and is now in the Iraq Museum in Baghdad; its own inscription records that it was carried off to Hattusa in 1595. The third class is estimate, and has to be discounted: the walled area of Babylon is commonly put at something like three hundred hectares, and the population of the city in the time of Hammurabi is estimated at anywhere from the tens of thousands to a hundred thousand; and there is no documentary basis whatever for the number of men in the Hittite expedition, estimates for the Old Kingdom army ranging from the thousands to the tens of thousands, with limited credibility.
cause: 打起來的原因有四層。表層是赫梯在南方的擴張：拉巴爾納奪取哈圖沙、穆爾希利把國都遷到內陸之後，赫梯人開始把勢力伸向幼發拉底河中游的敘利亞城邦，阿勒頗與哈蘇瓦先後落入其手，於是巴比倫的北翼直接變成赫梯的前線。深一層是巴比倫自身的僵局：阿摩利特王朝在薩姆杜—伊塔納之後對河中游的控制力轉弱，王室連年遠征消耗，加喜特人又在東面邊境上步步逼近，赫梯的推進對巴比倫而言已是既成事實。另一層是宗教與象徵的驅力：馬爾杜克是自稱統治天地的城神，其神像是巴比倫王權合法性的核心，奪走神像既是獵奇式的戰利品，也是宣示天命所歸的神學宣告——赫梯人不是要把巴比倫併入版圖，而是要取走這尊像、帶回哈圖沙，昭告天下誰才是神明的寵兒。最後是技術與制度層面的現實：赫梯是尚武的部族聯盟，沒有管理兩河灌溉農業的制度與人力，遠征軍只能停留一個作戰季；巴比倫則有城牆、神廟與龐大的城市人口，短期內無法被消化。於是雙方的選項其實很窄：巴比倫守住幼發拉底河中游，赫梯取走神像後退回安納托利亞。
causeEn: The reasons lie in four layers. At the surface is the Hittite expansion to the south: after Labarna took Hattusa and Mursili moved the capital inland, the Hittites began to extend their power over the Syrian city-states of the middle Euphrates, Aleppo and Hassuwa falling into their hands in turn, so that the northern flank of Babylon became the Hittite front directly. A layer deeper is the paralysis of Babylon itself: after Samsu-ditana the Amorite dynasty's grip on the middle river weakened, the royal house was worn down by repeated campaigns, and the Kassites were pressing in from the eastern frontier, so that the Hittite advance was for Babylon an accomplished fact. Another layer is religious and symbolic. Marduk was the city god who claimed dominion over heaven and earth, and his image was the core of the legitimacy of the Babylonian kingship; taking the image was at once a trophy of curiosity and a theological declaration that the Mandate of Heaven had shifted — the Hittites had no intention of annexing Babylonia, only of carrying the statue off to Hattusa and announcing to the world who now enjoyed the favour of the gods. Last are the constraints of technique and institution. The Hittites were a warlike tribal confederation without the institutions or the manpower to administer the irrigated agriculture of the two rivers, and an expeditionary army could stay for one campaigning season only; Babylon, with its walls, its temples and its great urban population, could not be absorbed in the short term either. The options on both sides were therefore narrow: Babylon would hold the middle Euphrates, and the Hittites would take the image and withdraw to Anatolia.
impact: 後果是分層的。最直接的一層是阿摩利特王朝在巴比倫的統治終結，隨後是札格羅斯山區的加喜特人入主王座，此後約四百四十年，巴比倫由一個外來王朝執掌。加喜特時期並非簡單的退步：它催生了所謂「加喜特風格」的圓雕與護符印藝術，興起了以王命刻辭的界石（庫杜魯）傳統，宮廷文書裡亞述語與加喜特語並用，巴比倫的宗教與藝術在衝突中混血。第二層是赫梯本身的命運：這場劫掠之後，赫梯人控制幼發拉底河上游與敘利亞約有一個世紀，卻在大約前1500年青銅時代普遍崩解中被摧毀，舊王國的輝煌與它剛剛搶走的戰利品一起消失；巴比倫之劫因此也說明，古代近東的王國可以在一個作戰季內決定勝負，也可以在下一個世紀裡灰飛煙滅。第三層是神像的往返：馬爾杜克神像大約在前1270年赫梯王圖庫爾提—尼努爾塔一世治下回到巴比倫，伊什塔爾銅像亦在十三世紀回返——哈圖沙的這份戰利品，最終還是以和平方式回到了原處。第四層是歷史記憶：此後亞述諸王的銘文把1595年的赫梯劫掠與更早的加喜特時期並列為前例，用來說明凡違逆神意而佔領巴比倫者，最終都會被神明驅逐；巴比倫之劫從此成為兩河世界「城可破、神像必返」的標準劇本。
impactEn: The consequences work in layers. The most direct is the end of Amorite rule at Babylon, and then the seating of the Kassites from the Zagros mountains on the throne, and for some four hundred and forty years afterwards Babylon was governed by a dynasty from outside. The Kassite period was not simply a decline: it brought the round sculpture and the seal impression style that goes by the name of the Kassite style, it raised the tradition of the kudurru, the boundary stone inscribed with royal commands, and it put Akkadian and Kassite side by side in the documents of the court, so that Babylonian religion and art were mixed by contact. The second layer is the fate of the Hittites themselves. For about a century after the sack they held the upper Euphrates and Syria, and then they were destroyed in the general collapse of the Bronze Age around 1500 BC, the glory of the Old Kingdom vanishing together with the plunder it had so recently seized; the sack of Babylon thus also shows that a kingdom in the ancient Near East could settle a war inside a single campaigning season and could be swept away in the next century. The third layer is the journey of the images. The statue of Marduk returned to Babylon about 1270 BC under the Hittite king Tukulti-Ninurta I, and the bronze Ishtar came back in the thirteenth century; the booty at Hattusa made its way home in the end, and by peace. The fourth layer is historical memory. Inscriptions of the Assyrian kings thereafter set the Hittite sack of 1595 alongside the still earlier Kassite period as precedents, to show that whoever seized Babylon against the will of the gods was in the end driven out by the gods; the sack of Babylon became, in the world of the two rivers, the standard scenario of a city that may be taken but whose god must return.
result: 公元前1595年的那一季，巴比倫被攻破：城區焚燒，王宮與神廟遭掠，馬爾杜克神像與西帕爾的伊什塔爾銅像被赫梯人運回哈圖沙，國王西布卡德—舒什從此下落不明，其不足一年的統治成了王朝的終點。《巴比倫王表A》在王朝之後直接接上加喜特人的接掌，編年文本也記下加喜特人入主與圖什拉塔的名字。第一巴比倫王朝就此終結，城市的政治秩序崩解，防務與灌溉的廢弛延續了數代人。赫梯人帶著戰利品退回安納托利亞，此後再未以君主身份統治美索不達米亞；對巴比倫而言，換來的既不是征服者，而是另一批主人——扎格羅斯來的加喜特人，把巴比倫的國王寶座重新扶上正統的名單，一直坐到前1155年被伊蘭的舒特魯克—納洪特攻破為止。從戰役本身看，這是一場乾淨利落的掠奪：沒有長久的圍城，沒有治理打算，只有一季的遠征、一場破城、一次帶著神像與抄本回家的路。
resultEn: In that campaigning season of 1595 BC Babylon was taken: the quarters were burned, the palace and the temples were stripped, the statue of Marduk and the bronze Ishtar of Sippar were carried off to Hattusa, and the king Sibkadd-Sheš disappeared from the record, his reign of less than a full year becoming the end of the dynasty. The Babylonian King List A passes straight from the dynasty to the accession of the Kassites, and the chronicle records the Kassite takeover and the name of Tushratta. The first Babylonian dynasty was over, the political order of the city broke down, and the neglect of the defences and of the irrigation went on for generations. The Hittites went back to Anatolia with their plunder and never ruled Mesopotamia again as kings; what they left Babylon was not a conqueror but a new set of masters, the Kassites from the Zagros, who set the Babylonian throne back on the list of legitimate kingdoms and kept it until 1155 BC, when Shutruk-Nahhunte of Elam broke it. Taken on its own terms the campaign was a clean sweep: no long siege, no intention of governing, only one season of marching, one storming of the city, and one road home with the images and the tablets.
